== Biography ==
{{Appalachia Sticker|born|state=Pennsylvania}}
 Hannah W. Glasgow; b. 4 Mar 1812 at Blair, Pennsylvania; 

m. John Sides Shoff, son of Christopher Shoff Sr. and Elizabeth Seitz, 1835 at Huntingdon, Huntingdon, Pennsylvania; d

She died 2 Feb 1898 at Clearfield, Clearfield, Pennsylvania, 85; Æ 85 years, 10 months and 29 days; she was buried at Crossroads Cemetery, Beccaria Township, Clearfield, Pennsylvania.

His obituary was published as follows:<br>
<center>Her obituary was published as follows:</center>
<div style="float:Center; border:2px #000 solid; background-color: #f7eed1; width:300px; height:auto; margin: auto">
Thursday morning, February 2nd, 1898, Mrs. Hannah Shoff died at the residence of her son Sides Shoff in Beccaria township, aged 85 years, 10 months and 29 days. Grip was the cause of her death. Mrs. Shoff's maiden name was Glasgow, a daughter of Mr. and Mrs. John Glasgow, who were among the earliest settlers of what is now Reade township in Cambria county. She was married to John Shoff, who preceded her to the grave about 33 years ago. She is survived by four daughters and four sons. The deceased had been a member of the Presbyterian church for 65 years. The funeral services were conducted on Sunday afternoon at 3 o'clock by the Presbyterian minister of Ramey, assisted by Rev. Hugh Strain of the M. E. church, Glen Hope, after which the remains were laid to rest in the Cross Roads cemetery. Undertaker Beers had charge of the remains.
</div>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-664]] is assessed at 95% (proved). Hannah’s 1898 obituary calls her a daughter of Mr.and Mrs.John Glasgow, early settlers of what became Reade Township, Cambria County. That distinctive locality agrees with the selected John’s 1820 Cambria household and her 1812/1813 birth.

Hannah Shoff as daughter of the John Glasgow described in the held 1898 obituary quotation. The newspaper title and original page remain unidentified; the 1850 married-household census is context, not father evidence. Maternity and John’s own ancestry remain unproved.

Next useful test: Recover the original 1898 obituary and John’s probate.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1187 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-1187]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
